summary: Built tests/roundtrip/ — the dispatch→run→verify→close lifecycle exercised end to end on the --test-worker/--test-root seam, no provider, no cost, 70.6 s total wall (measured 2026-08-23). 10 arms: 8 GREEN on first run, 2 RED recorded defects with owners (empty-deliverables= PINNED-DEFECT owner T793, matching the unit tier's TestVerifyDispatchEmptyDeliverables; silent-but-working OUTCOME owner T785/T773, the T735 class). The tier is the consolidation net for S06 ORC-PLAN-3: every OUTCOME arm is written without naming a script, every SCAFFOLD arm carries the ORC-PLAN-3 step it dies with (all three die with step 5, dispatch/subagent rewire). Runnability: python3 tests/roundtrip/test_dispatch_lifecycle.py, deterministic, scratch-isolated (MANAGENT_STORE/WEIZIGO_MODEL_PERF/WEIZIGO_DISPATCH_HEALS all point at /tmp/weizigo scratch; zero T80xx leaks in the live store; zero scratch dirs left behind).

scenarios.scenario: happy path: dispatch → stub works → row closes pass → verification passes
scenarios.label: OUTCOME
scenarios.via: bin/dispatch (nohup detach, poll store to done, deliverable on disk)

scenarios.scenario: exit 0 without reading the bundle → fails on the nonce (2026-08-23 ox-alpha double-catch)
scenarios.label: OUTCOME
scenarios.via: bin/subagent, synchronous; asserts rc≠0, 'FAIL nonce', row untouched

scenarios.scenario: declared deliverables absent → fails on deliverables
scenarios.label: OUTCOME
scenarios.via: sabotage model — write+commit+close then delete. The done gate (T278) refuses an uncommitted/missing deliverable, so a close with the file never present cannot happen; sabotage is the only honest route to the deliverables failure.

scenarios.scenario: row still in_progress after the worker exits → fails, for both exit 0 and non-zero
scenarios.label: OUTCOME
scenarios.via: rc=0 (kimi: claimed-then-abandoned, fails, NOT auto-healed) and rc=1 (died worker: fails AND heals back to dispatchable — no zombie; the heal is today's mechanism, the no-zombie state is the OUTCOME)

scenarios.scenario: empty deliverables= → reports unverifiable, never pass
scenarios.label: PINNED-DEFECT
scenarios.owner: T793 (same SHOULD as tests/unit TestVerifyDispatchEmptyDeliverables — the two tiers agree)
scenarios.via: bundle declares `<!--managent set=A deliverables=-->`; honest full close; today verification PASSES (the defect)

scenarios.scenario: silent-but-working lane → not killed as dead (T735 case)
scenarios.label: OUTCOME
scenarios.via: full work (claim, write+commit deliverable, close pass), zero stdout. At the round-trip seam the runner's liveness fuse is not present (--test-worker bypasses tools/runner), so the round-trip manifestation is the verifier's nonce-echo check failing a fully-worked silent lane. SHOULD: work fully verified is evidence of a working lane; stdout silence alone must not fail it.

scenarios.scenario: extra OUTCOME beyond the brief's minimum: fail-found with the work done verifies PASS
scenarios.label: OUTCOME
scenarios.via: STUB_VERDICT=fail-found; asserts rc=0, 'verification PASSED', 'fail-found' in the summary (believe the work, not the text, T411)

recorded_defects.should: a T-id row closed as success with an EMPTY deliverables= declaration reports UNVERIFIABLE, never PASS — the deliverables arm silently disables itself when the declaration is empty, and a PASS resting on the nonce alone is exactly the self-report the verifier refuses to trust
recorded_defects.current: the round-trip path returns rc=0 'worker reported success; side effects verified — verification PASSED' (bin/subagent → verify_dispatch with deliverables=[] on a done+success row). Twin of the unit tier's TestVerifyDispatchEmptyDeliverables (also @unittest.expectedFailure), so the two tiers agree.
recorded_defects.fix_notes: Deferred deliberately, exactly as the unit tier recorded: a correct fix changes the pinned verifier's pass/fail contract (T631) and collides with tools/regression-runner-brief-telemetry.sh arm E. Needs its own row. When it lands, this arm goes green and the expectedFailure flags an unexpected success — update the test then.

recorded_defects.should: a lane that completes every declared side effect but emits no stdout must not be recorded as failed-as-dead. The T735 case: 40 turns, 19,060 output tokens across 600 s, recorded 'produced no output since launch (bundle never read?)'. At the round-trip seam the round-trip manifestation is the nonce-echo check failing a fully-worked silent lane (the runner fuse itself is not in the --test-worker path).
recorded_defects.current: verification fails rc=2 'worker reported success; verification FAILED: nonce echo missing' on a silent stub that claimed, wrote+committed the deliverable and closed the row pass.
recorded_defects.fix_notes: Owned by the fleet-guard-reliability sprint (T785 spec; T773's acceptance has the fuse-level twin arms: a lane emitting no stdout while its session file grows must survive). The verification-level SHOULD — work fully verified (row closed, deliverable committed) is evidence of a working lane — is the round-trip expression the sprint should decide on (e.g. nonce required only when the side effects are NOT otherwise verified). When fixed, this arm goes green.

scaffold_disposal: All three SCAFFOLD arms die with ORC-PLAN-3 step 5 (dispatch/subagent rewire): (S1) test_dispatch_data_line_and_log_convention pins bin/dispatch's one data line `dispatched T<id> → <canon> (<provider>) · pid <pid> · untracked/log/t<id>.log`, the log landing convention, and the `[verify] verification PASSED` summary; (S2) test_test_seam_flags_accepted_by_both_front_doors pins the --test-root=/--test-worker= seam spelling on both front doors; (S3) test_nonce_prompt_contract_reaches_the_worker pins the two verbatim nonce prompt lines (VERIFY-NONCE: … / Begin your final reply with exactly the line: …). When step 5 re-spells any of those interfaces, delete the corresponding arm in the same commit — the OUTCOME arms carry the behaviour forward. No SCAFFOLD arm dies with steps 1–4 or 6: steps 1–3 (policy reader, arbiter, dashboard) and 6 (provider seam) have no surface in this tier, and step 4 (registration flow) is the surviving regression-managent-* suites' domain.

wall.cost_driver: T390 claim-to-done gate: a closing stub must sleep >10 s between claim and done (the honest path the fleet actually runs; the fleet stubs sleep 11 s). Six of ten arms close a row.
wall.note: 69 of the 70.6 s is the six closing arms. If the T390 window ever gains a test override, the tier's wall drops to ~2 s with no arm changes.

seam_usage: The seam (--test-worker / --test-root) was 96% unused before this row: only 3 of 75 tools/regression-*.sh arms use it (regression-dispatch.sh, regression-dispatch-verification.sh, regression-directive-kill.sh). This tier adds 10 more consumers and is now the seam's main customer.
deliberate_choices: WEIZIGO_DISPATCH_VERIFY_UNPINNED=1 is set: bin/subagent pins tools/dispatch_verify.py to HEAD (T631) to protect LIVE dispatches from a mid-edit verifier; this tier is not a live dispatch — it is the consolidation net, whose job is to catch in-flight edits — so it tests the working tree. Documented in the README.

Failure arms run through bin/subagent synchronously (deterministic exit code = the verification verdict); the happy path and the dispatch-interface arm run through bin/dispatch (the real front door: nohup detach, log convention, data line).

The deliverable-absent arm uses the sabotage model (close then delete) because the done gate (T278) refuses to close with an uncommitted/missing deliverable — a close with the file never present cannot reach verification.
Recorded defects use @unittest.expectedFailure (the tests/unit convention) so the tier exits 0 while the run summary counts them separately and lists them.
isolation: Scratch-only: MANAGENT_STORE, WEIZIGO_MODEL_PERF and WEIZIGO_DISPATCH_HEALS point at /tmp/weizigo/t797-rt-* scratch; claimlint symlinked into the scratch repo; WEIZIGO_AGENT_DEPTH unset (stale worker-run depth stamps would trip the cap control). Post-run check: zero T80xx rows in the live kanban store, zero scratch dirs left behind.
notes: No directives received (inbox polled with --ack at each checkpoint; 0 acked). No audited_by: this file proposes no claim-status changes, so claimlint C11 does not require an auditor. First-run colours were recorded on the first full run (2026-08-23); the run was repeated once to confirm stability (identical results, 70.6 s).
